react_result.final_narrative_text: The treatment-vs-control differential metabolome converges powerfully on the arachidonic acid eicosanoid cascade. Across three independent enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA, mummichog m/z-direct network activity, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA — the top-ranked pathway is Eicosanoid synthesis / Arachidonic acid metabolism (WP:WP167; KEGG:hsa00590), with FDR = 1.25 × 10⁻¹³ (RaMP) and p = 0.00378 (mummichog). Five driver metabolites are shared across these results: arachidonic acid (C00219), Leukotriene A4 (C00909), 5-HETE (C04805), 15-HETE (C04742), and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-prostaglandin J2 (C14717). Arachidonic acid is the obligate substrate; 5-lipoxygenase (ALOX5) converts it to Leukotriene A4 and subsequently to the 5(S)-HETE series, while cytochrome-P450 and COX/LOX routes generate 15(S)-HETE and the cyclopentenone prostaglandin 15d-PGJ2. The extraordinary fold-enrichment of 1,429 in RaMP reflects the high specificity of this lipid signal. Histamine (C00388) independently maps to KEGG histidine metabolism (hsa00340; p = 0.068) in MetaboAnalystR, suggesting a secondary histaminergic component. Dihydrothymine (C00906) is a pyrimidine catabolite with no pathway partners in the differential set. Hypochlorite, copper, and gentisic acid were not significantly enriched in any paradigm. The biological story is one of systemic activation of the arachidonic acid–derived eicosanoid network, consistent with inflammatory, oxidative-stress, or pharmacological perturbation.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three pathway-analysis paradigms converged on arachidonic acid metabolism as the dominant affected network in this differential metabolome. RaMP-DB ORA returned Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the top hit with FDR 1.25e-13, driven by five input metabolites (arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 5-HETE, 15-HETE, and 15-deoxy-delta-12,14-PGJ2). Mummichog m/z-direct analysis ranked Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) first (p = 0.000168), with the same four canonical eicosanoid compounds resolving into the network. MetaboAnalystR PSEA against KEGG identified hsa00590 Arachidonic acid metabolism as the top pathway (p = 2.49e-06), matching four of the same driver metabolites. Arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219) is the obligate upstream substrate in all three hits, feeding into the leukotriene branch via ALOX5 and into the HETE branch via ALOX5 and CYP450 monooxygenases. The cyclopentenone prostaglandin 15-deoxy-delta-12,14-PGJ2 extends the downstream eicosanoid output. The remaining input compounds (histamine, dihydrothymine, gentisic acid, copper, and hypochlorite) did not map to enriched pathways across any paradigm.

pathway_members.sqlite only indexes HUMAN1 + RECON2; for namespace 'WP', inspect the `metabolites_hit` list inside an EnrichmentResult (e.g. from run_ramp_enrichment) — it carries the method-specific compound roster

  "narrative_text": "The treatment-vs-control differential metabolome converges powerfully on the arachidonic acid eicosanoid cascade. Across three independent enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA, mummichog m/z-direct network activity, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA — the top-ranked pathway is Eicosanoid synthesis / Arachidonic acid metabolism (WP:WP167; KEGG:hsa00590), with FDR = 1.25 × 10⁻¹³ (RaMP) and p = 0.00378 (mummichog). Five driver metabolites are shared across these results: arachidonic acid (C00219), Leukotriene A4 (C00909), 5-HETE (C04805), 15-HETE (C04742), and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-prostaglandin J2 (C14717). Arachidonic acid is the obligate substrate; 5-lipoxygenase (ALOX5) converts it to Leukotriene A4 and subsequently to the 5(S)-HETE series, while cytochrome-P450 and COX/LOX routes generate 15(S)-HETE and the cyclopentenone prostaglandin 15d-PGJ2. The extraordinary fold-enrichment of 1,429 in RaMP reflects the high specificity of this lipid signal. Histamine (C00388) independently maps to KEGG histidine metabolism (hsa00340; p = 0.068) in MetaboAnalystR, suggesting a secondary histaminergic component. Dihydrothymine (C00906) is a pyrimidine catabolite with no pathway partners in the differential set. Hypochlorite, copper, and gentisic acid were not significantly enriched in any paradigm. The biological story is one of systemic activation of the arachidonic acid–derived eicosanoid network, consistent with inflammatory, oxidative-stress, or pharmacological perturbation.",

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The treatment-vs-control differential metabolome converges powerfully on the arachidonic acid eicosanoid cascade. Across three independent enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA, mummichog m/z-direct network activity, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA — the top-ranked pathway is Eicosanoid synthesis / Arachidonic acid metabolism (WP:WP167; KEGG:hsa00590), with FDR = 1.25 × 10⁻¹³ (RaMP) and p = 0.00378 (mummichog). Five driver metabolites are shared across these results: arachidonic acid (C00219), Leukotriene A4 (C00909), 5-HETE (C04805), 15-HETE (C04742), and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-prostaglandin J2 (C14717). Arachidonic acid is the obligate substrate; 5-lipoxygenase (ALOX5) converts it to Leukotriene A4 and subsequently to the 5(S)-HETE series, while cytochrome-P450 and COX/LOX routes generate 15(S)-HETE and the cyclopentenone prostaglandin 15d-PGJ2. The extraordinary fold-enrichment of 1,429 in RaMP reflects the high specificity of this lipid signal. Histamine (C00388) independently maps to KEGG histidine metabolism (hsa00340; p = 0.068) in MetaboAnalystR, suggesting a secondary histaminergic component. Dihydrothymine (C00906) is a pyrimidine catabolite with no pathway partners in the differential set. Hypochlorite, copper, and gentisic acid were not significantly enriched in any paradigm. The biological story is one of systemic activation of the arachidonic acid–derived eicosanoid network, consistent with inflammatory, oxidative-stress, or pharmacological perturbation.
